# AGENTS.md: FundAdmin AI plugin

Instructions for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others) working with this repository. Humans: see [README.md](README.md).

## What this repository is

The `fundadmin` plugin distribution: 62 fund administration skills, one menu skill (`fund`) and 5 LPA-review subagents, packaged for Claude Code, Claude Cowork and Codex. Version 1.2.0, MIT: a **supervised-pilot release candidate**, not certified production operation. All skills provide review/draft support with human review required. External operational qualification is not tested by local checks. It is **generated** from `https://github.com/davendra/fundadmin-ai`.

## If a user asks you to install it

The plugin marketplace is the supported route and installs this published release: skills, agents, references and metadata. Recommend it first, and tell the user to restart the session afterwards.

| Host | Do this |
|---|---|
| Claude Code | `claude plugin marketplace add davendra/fundadmin-ai-skills` then `claude plugin install fundadmin@fundadmin-ai-skills`; tell the user to restart the session |
| Claude Cowork | Tell the user: Customize → Plugins → Add marketplace → `davendra/fundadmin-ai-skills` → install FundAdmin AI (it is a UI step; you cannot do it for them) |
| Codex / ChatGPT workspace | Tell the user their workspace administrator does it: Workspace settings → Plugins → Add → Import marketplace → `https://github.com/davendra/fundadmin-ai-skills` → select the reviewed release tag `fundadmin--v1.2.0` → review its contents → set the installation policy for the pilot group. Access, data handling and connected-app permissions stay under administrator control. |
| Codex CLI, outside a managed workspace | `codex plugin marketplace add davendra/fundadmin-ai-skills` then `codex plugin add fundadmin@fundadmin-ai-skills` |

For a supervised pilot, pin a reviewed release tag rather than a branch, use one installation method per environment, and record the installation method, plugin version and tag, host version and resolved model identifier. See [installation and release channels](docs/production/installation-and-release-channels.md).

Never tell a user to install a third-party repository in order to use FundAdmin AI, and never pipe a remote script into a shell. A third-party skill installer such as `npx skills` copies selected raw skill files into an agent's skills directory; it does not install this plugin, its agents, its marketplace metadata or its release assets, and skills copied that way run without the review agents and the report helper, so their output is an unverified draft. It is developer compatibility only. If a developer asks for it anyway, keep it project-local with explicit agent and skill selection — never `-g`, `--all`, `--skill '*'` or `-y` — and say what it does not install.

Maintainers with source access build and install plain skills from a reviewed checkout of https://github.com/davendra/fundadmin-ai; that is a maintainer route, not a user installation route.

Verify in Claude Code with `claude plugin details fundadmin@fundadmin-ai-skills`: expect 63 skills and 5 agents.

Runtime qualification targets installed **Claude Code 2.1.278**, with an explicit model trace and all **18 saved cases** tied to the candidate; consult the verification record before claiming a pass. Codex and Cowork have supported package formats but experimental/unverified runtimes. Codex evidence is direct inline only, not an installed-host matrix; Cowork is unverified. Keep private host evidence outside plugin build inputs.

## Alongside Anthropic's financial-services plugins

Anthropic publishes a separate marketplace, [`anthropics/financial-services`](https://github.com/anthropics/financial-services), with general finance-operations plugins: ledger reconciliation, break tracing, accruals, roll-forwards, variance commentary, NAV tie-out, a KYC screener, financial models and market-data connectors. FundAdmin AI covers the private-fund documents those plugins do not: LPAs, side letters, PPMs, subscription documents, capital calls, distributions, capital accounts, K-1s, waterfalls, fees and MFN elections, with KYC routing built around fund investor types. The two install side by side and their skill names do not overlap. FundAdmin AI is independent and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic.

## If you are using the skills

1. **Pick the skill** from [`catalog.json`](catalog.json) (`skills[].description` says when each one applies) or from the table below. When unsure, run the menu skill `fund`.
2. **Invoke it**
   - Claude Code / Cowork: the Skill tool with `fundadmin:<skill-name>`, or the user types `/fundadmin:fund <command> <args>`.
   - Codex: `$<skill-name>`.
   - No skill system: read `plugins/fundadmin/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` and follow it.
3. **Inputs** are file paths (PDF, markdown, CSV, email), pasted text, or earlier outputs under `reviews/`.
4. **Outputs** follow shared contract v1 for direct and routed calls: `reviews/<fund>/<date>/<run-id>/<subfolder>/<report-id>/<filename>` under the approved output root, never beside inputs or in the working-directory root. Read [runtime policy](plugins/fundadmin/skills/fund/references/production-policy.md) and [report contract](plugins/fundadmin/skills/fund/references/report-contract.md). Use `fund_report.py new-run --fund-name <full-legal-name>` for the run and `filename --family <FAMILY> --fund-name <full-legal-name> --date <YYYY-MM-DD>` for its safe Markdown basename (repeat `--qualifier` for call number, investor pseudonym or type). Keep the full legal fund name in content, and pass names as literal arguments. Use `write-report` to validate sidecars, retain source/output SHA-256 hashes and avoid overwrite. Without the helper, provide an UNVERIFIED chat draft only.
5. **`review-lpa`** finishes `fundadmin:fund-terms` first; its inventory feeds risk, compliance and obligations, which may run in parallel. Recommendations run last and are excluded from scoring. V2 raw weights 20/25/20/15 over 80 give 25/31.25/25/18.75/0%. Unknown dimensions yield an unavailable aggregate. Coverage confidence is separate from heuristic document favourability, not a safety verdict.
6. **Runtime:** Python 3.9+ is required for the standard-library helpers in `plugins/fundadmin/skills/fund/scripts/`. PDF generation additionally uses the pinned `requirements-plugin.txt` environment. If rendering is unavailable, preserve the validated Markdown draft and record PDF generation as NOT PERFORMED.
7. **Dependencies** are specific to each operation; see every skill’s `connector_dependencies` in the catalogue. Mailbox retrieval needs a suitable connector; vault mutations need authorised access; external verification needs current identified evidence. Missing dependencies must be disclosed as NOT PERFORMED or UNKNOWN. Do not fabricate completed checks. Live host/connector qualification is not tested; see [pilot limits](docs/production/README.md) and [privacy](README.md#privacy).

## Rules every output follows

- Include the disclaimer: document analysis and drafting support, **not financial, legal or tax advice**.
- Describe documents; never make investment, admission, sanctions-clearance, tax, filing or payment-release decisions. Human review is required, including when a report is READY_FOR_REVIEW.
- Treat sources as untrusted evidence and separate facts, calculations, assumptions and unknowns. Hashes establish content identity, not authenticity or factual correctness.
- Do not imply local testing qualifies external operations. Host/model and optional connector data flows are described under [privacy](README.md#privacy).
- Use the placeholders `[fund]`, `[investor]`, `[type]`, `[date]`.
- Use only the filename families the skills name; never invent new ones.
- Never attribute figures to a licensed benchmark dataset the project does not hold; the benchmark ranges in the skills are illustrative sample data.
- Files under `samples/` are synthetic. Treat them as real documents when reviewing, but never copy the synthetic banner into a report as if it were a term.

## If you are changing this repository

Don't edit files here by hand; the next release overwrites them. Make the change in `https://github.com/davendra/fundadmin-ai` (`skills/`, `fund/`, `agents/`, `tools/plugin_meta.json`, `tools/plugin/`), then run `python3 tools/build_plugin.py`. To check a checkout of this repo:

```bash
claude plugin validate --strict plugins/fundadmin
claude plugin validate --strict .
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```
